newsitem.title: USA: Court orders Dow implant cases consolidated.
newsitem.headline: Court orders Dow implant cases consolidated.

text.p: A U.S. appeals court Thursday ruled that about 14,000 breast implant cases naming Dow Chemical Co. as a defendant should be consolidated in U.S. Disrict Court in Detroit.

The decision by the Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals in Cincinnati could save Dow Chemical from fighting costly legal battles in courts across the country, but a state court judge in New Orleans Thursday refused to terminate an implant trial already in progress.

Dow Chemical, based in Midland, Mich., owns 50 percent of Dow Corning Inc., which was once the nation's largest manufacturer of silicone-gel breast implants. The consolidation ruling also applies to Dow Corning's other shareholder, Corning Inc., which has been named in far fewer lawsuits.

Since Dow Corning filed for bankruptcy protection two years ago -- freezing litigation against it -- many women have pursued breast implant-related health claims against Dow Chemical, which did some silicone testing on behalf of Dow Corning in the 1950s and 60s.
Hundreds of thousands of women have claimed that their silicone-gel breast implants are responsible for various health problems, including lupus and rheumatoid arthritis.

The Sixth Circuit appeals court ordered in July 1996 that cases against Dow Corning be consolidated. In Thursday's decision, Dow Chemical had argued that Dow Corning's resources would be depleted and its bankruptcy reorganization delayed if its two shareholders were forced to fight thousands of individual lawsuits.
The three judge appeals panel agreed, saying that consolidation of the cases was the best way to preserve Dow Corning's assets and provide quick adjudication of claims.
"Dow Corning's assets are finite, and risk being unnecessarily diminished by the expense of litigating thousands of breast implant claims in innumerable jursdictions," the judges wrote.
But Judge Yada McGee in Orleans Parish Civil Court in Louisiana, told attorneys on Thursday she will not halt testimony in the first implant trial against Dow Chemical, now in its fifth week.
McGee cited a 1995 ruling by the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals that ordered the New Orleans case to proceed to trial.

The U.S. District Court in Detroit "probably will look at this but it should not disrupt this case procedurally or substantively," said Dawn Barrios, one of the plaintiff's attorneys in the New Orleans case.
